turns.text: What stood out today?
We turned on typo tolerance in help search for everyone today. Empty searches went from about 1,500 a day to under 900 a day. I built it and ran the rollout myself.

metrics.source_text: Empty searches went from about 1,500 a day to under 900 a day

turns.text: How did today go?
Eh, worked on stuff. The import mostly. Some meetings.
What part of the import did you get done?
Just poking at it honestly, nothing finished really.
What stood out today?
Today was all mentoring. I sat with the junior for most of the afternoon on their first real feature, and I reviewed a plan a new hire wrote. No code from me at all.
What changed for them?
The junior said they finally get how we put changes live, and the new hire rewrote their plan after my comments.
What did you get done?
I changed the import so it saves articles in batches instead of one by one. It went from about 20 to 80 articles a second, so like 4x.

metrics.source_text: It went from about 20 to 80 articles a second

turns.text: How did the move to the new article format go?
It finished. We moved about 9k help articles over to the new format without the help centre going down.
What stood out today?
I helped a teammate figure out the flaky search tests. They did most of the fixing, I mainly spotted that the tests were using the real clock instead of a fixed time.
You added caching to search today. Did it get faster?
It feels a lot faster, but honestly I don't know the number. I didn't check the dashboard.
How did the import change go?
The import change went well. It's about 40% faster now.
Was that something you led?
Yes, I led it, I wrote the plan and did the rollout.
How are you doing today?
Tired. I was on call and got woken up at 3 am because the help centre was really slow. One stuck search was blocking everything else, I stopped it and we were back to normal in about 25 minutes.
How did it end?
Fine in the end. Nobody lost anything. I'm just wiped.

metrics.source_text: we were back to normal in about 25 minutes

turns.text: What stood out today?
The team launched the new contact us page in the help centre. I wrote the help text for it.
Any early results?
Not yet, it's only been a day.
Anything you learned today?

I learned why the assistant sometimes makes up an answer when it can't find a matching article, it has to be told it's okay to say it doesn't know. Also my lead said my write-up was the clearest one this quarter, which was nice.
What happened today?
I'm blocked. The test server is down and the other team says it won't be back until Thursday, so I can't try out the import change.
What will you do tomorrow then?
Tomorrow I'll write the plan for undoing the change instead, so it's ready if something goes wrong.
What stood out today?

I cut how long our tests take before each release. They used to take 14 minutes and now it's around 6. I made them reuse files they'd already downloaded and split them into 4 groups that run at the same time.

metrics.source_text: They used to take 14 minutes and now it's around 6

turns.text: How did today go?
Long day. Had a tough conversation with a teammate who felt left out of the search decisions, and we agreed they'd run the next planning review.
How did they take it?
Better than I expected. They thanked me after.
Before we start, one from yesterday: how many search alerts fired per week before and after the threshold change?
I checked, we went from about 40 alerts a week to 6.
Great. What stood out today?
We decided the import should save its progress as it goes, so if it crashes halfway it picks up where it stopped instead of starting over. I pushed for it.

metrics.source_text: we went from about 40 alerts a week to 6
